QA Strategy Template

This document has been created for QA as a starting point for facilitating QA processes in a new or existing project. Points 1–4 about the quadrants, along with their related subpoints, should be documented in a shared workspace for the relevant team. There will also most likely be continuous updates as the team and its processes evolve.

Use this QA Strategy Template to document the outcome from the QA insight template. The purpose of documenting the work process is to make visible how things are today, as well as to uncover further ambitions for improvement. Use the main chapters from the QA insight template and the figure below as a starting point.

A picture containing text, font, circle, screenshot

Also include what the Definition of Ready (DoR) and Definition of Done (DoD) are in the different columns in the work board.

The following tables are used to map the team’s status in different aspects of QA, as well as ambitions for where the team wants to be in these aspects. The columns are filled out based on input from the team and discussions with QA, the team lead, and possibly the product owner.

This part of the document is a support tool for QA, and links to a document that can be used to gain insight into the project status: QA strategy insight questions.

Findings and actions

Summarize risks, opportunities for improvement, and actions. Divide them into severity categories:

    Critical
    High
    Medium
    Low

Then divide them into:

    Actions you can take yourself
    Actions you should propose to the team
    Actions that require anchoring with a manager / product / technical owner

Note: Avoid initiating too many actions at once. Make an assessment and start where it makes the most sense based on the findings.
Examples:

    Make unit testing a fixed routine or part of onboarding for new developers.
    User Story and Bug template with required fields.
    Reassess DoD and DoR and create checkboxes (link to Sayyar’s examples for DoD/DoR).
    Clarify roles and expectations.

Present

Give the team a summarized presentation of the current status. Let the team contribute to filling in ambitions and actions. This gives the team ownership of quality and actions, while also placing QA in a leading role within its discipline.
Follow up and measure improvements

    Follow up to ensure that the actions are actually carried out.
    Measure the effect (test coverage, number of defects, build time, quality of backlog, etc.)
    Document the learnings
    Adjust the process further as needed

This ensures continuous improvement and documents the value of QA.

Here, for example, you can define actions as work items on the team’s board or backlog.
